contacto.subtitulo: Do you have any questions, suggestions, or want to register your establishment? We are here to help.
contacto.ubicacion_desc: Independencia No. 12, Centro, Jalpan de Serra, Qro. CP 76340

contacto.faq_subtitulo: Everything you need to know about registering and using the platform.
contacto.mas_dudas: Do you have more questions? Write to us directly using the form above.
contacto.faq_1_q: Requirements to register on the platform?
contacto.faq_1_a: Basic requirements include having a gastronomic establishment located in Jalpan de Serra, having the corresponding municipal permits, and providing complete and truthful information about your business.
contacto.faq_2_q: Is there any cost to use the site?
contacto.faq_2_a: No, the site is completely free for all visitors. Its goal is to showcase the food, lodging and experiences of Jalpan de Serra.
contacto.faq_3_q: Can I update my establishment's information?
contacto.faq_3_a: Yes, once your establishment is registered, you will have access to a personal panel where you can update all information, including menu, hours, photos, and contact details in real-time.
contacto.faq_4_q: How can customers find my establishment?
contacto.faq_4_a: Customers can find your establishment through a search by name, type of food, location, or by using the filters available on the home page.

ij.hero_sub: The heart of the Sierra Gorda: missions, rivers and mountain cooking.
ij.dato1: Work begins on the Santiago Mission, led by Friar Junípero Serra
ij.dato2: The Sierra Gorda is declared a Biosphere Reserve
ij.dato3: Its Franciscan missions become a UNESCO World Heritage Site
ij.dato4: Jalpan is named a Pueblo Mágico (Magical Town)
ij.imp1_d: The first of the five Sierra Gorda missions, built between 1751 and 1758.
ij.imp2_d: An old presidio facing the square that tells the region's story.
ij.imp3_d: The bandstand, the Jalpan letters and evenings in the garden.
ij.imp4_d: Flowers, crafts, piñatas and local snacks.
ij.imp5_d: Giant cypress trees and calm water minutes from downtown.
ij.imp6_d: Thick-walled mansions, cobblestone streets and lanterns for an unhurried stroll.
ij.imp7_d: Kayaks, pedal boats and sunsets among submerged trees, minutes from downtown.
ij.imp8_d: Stalactites, stalagmites and light streaming in from the top of the cave.
ij.imp9_d: Dirt roads through orchards, stone fences and green hills.
ij.imp10_d: Santa María del Agua de Landa: a baroque façade full of reliefs and saints.
ij.imp11_d: Our Lady of Light of Tancoyol, tucked away in the mountains.
ij.imp12_d: San Miguel Concá, the smallest of the five, in a warm valley.
ij.imp13_d: San Francisco del Valle de Tilaco, surrounded by mountains.
ij.sab_d: In the market and small eateries you taste the sierra: cecina, enchiladas serranas, zacahuil and village bread. And on every corner, clay, palm and embroidery made here.
ij.llegar_title: See you in the Sierra Gorda
ij.llegar_1: About three and a half hours from Querétaro city on federal highway 120.
ij.llegar_2: Warm weather most of the year; bring sunscreen and water.
